perspective:
Jose has access to the following:

- He works at/around a community bank, occasionally helping with maintenance and repairs, and knows Patricia Ndiaye as a bank teller colleague. They have a friendly, professional relationship.
- He noticed Patricia seemed more withdrawn and less vibrant than usual during shifts, and he suspected something might be troubling her.
- He asked if she was okay. Patricia said it was “nothing really, just some personal stuff,” thanked him for asking, and said his offer to listen meant a lot.
- During a lunch break, he overheard Patricia on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- He told her he’d been reading about financial planning strategies and offered to discuss them. Patricia said she’d been overwhelmed with bills lately and might take him up on it.
- Afterward, he worried he might have overstepped by bringing up finances. He told Patricia he didn’t mean to pry. She said she didn’t think he was prying and was grateful for his offer.
- He told her he respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend. Patricia said she appreciated having someone to turn to.
- Later, he checked in with her about her weekend. Patricia said she was fine and planned a quiet weekend at home. He offered to be there if she needed anything. She thanked him and said she’d keep that in mind.
- He continued checking in with her at work. Patricia said she was busy but handling it, thanked him, and said it was great to have his support.
- He got the sense that Patricia appreciated his concern but preferred to handle her personal issues privately.
